title: Code Reviewer cf-sandbox API, version 1
description:
The HTTP API between the Dispatcher (`dispatcher/src/launchers/cf-sandbox.ts`, issue #1158) and the Cloudflare Worker `cr-sandbox` (`cloudflare/sandbox/`, issue #1159): one Durable Object and one Cloudflare Container (a microVM) per VM. It is the Dispatcher's port `SandboxService` + `SandboxFleet` (`dispatcher/src/launchers/sandbox-service.ts`) over HTTPS. Every request except `GET /health` carries `Authorization: Bearer <CF_SANDBOX_TOKEN>` (at least 32 characters, compared in constant time); a missing or wrong one is `401` with no body detail. JSON in and out. An error is `{"error": <SandboxFailureKind>}` (`ErrorResponse`) with the matching status: 400 `rejected`, 401 `auth_failed`, 404 `not_ready`, 429 `rate_limited`, 503 `unavailable`; the text of any other failure is never sent. A reader ignores fields it does not know. The paths are in `Paths` below (JSON Schema has no place for them): `POST /v1/vms` (CreateVmRequest -> 201 CreateVmResponse), `POST /v1/vms/{name}/exec` (ExecRequest -> 200 ExecResponse), `POST /v1/vms/{name}/processes` (StartProcessRequest -> 201 StartProcessResponse; the process outlives the HTTP request), `POST /v1/vms/{name}/processes/{id}/stdin` (StdinRequest -> 204), `POST /v1/vms/{name}/processes/{id}/stdin/close` (no body -> 204), `GET /v1/vms/{name}/processes/{id}?waitMs=<0..25000>` (-> 200 ProcessState, answered when the process ended or after waitMs), `PUT /v1/vms/{name}/network` (NetworkRequest -> 204, effective for the next request the VM makes), `DELETE /v1/vms/{name}` (-> 204; a VM that is gone or never existed is not an error), `GET /v1/vms?namePrefix=&tag=k:v` (-> 200 ListVmsResponse; one tag at most), `GET /health` (no auth -> 200 HealthResponse). A VM ends by itself at its `timeoutMs` (the Durable Object's alarm destroys the Container).

What the image must hold, so that the Dispatcher's VM steps (the ones of the Vercel golden snapshot, `docs/runner.md` "Cloudflare placement") work unchanged: `/usr/local/sbin/vm-prepare.sh` and `/usr/local/sbin/sysbox-prepare.sh` (as in the golden snapshot), Docker with the Worker image loaded under the tag `code-reviewer-worker:golden`, `mkfs.ext4`, `fallocate`, `mount`. `POST /v1/vms` answers 201 only after the image's own boot is done: the intercept CA of the outbound handler (`/etc/cloudflare/certs/cloudflare-containers-ca.crt`, which Cloudflare writes when the Container starts) is in the system store, so `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` of the VM holds the public roots and that CA. The Dispatcher binds that one file, read-only, over the same path in the Worker container and sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` to it. `HealthResponse.workerImageDigest` is the image id (`sha256:...`) of the Worker image in the Container image, which the Dispatcher compares with `docker image inspect` in the VM (`image_mismatch` otherwise), and `sysboxProof` is `proven` only when the image's build proved the patched Sysbox the way the golden snapshot's record does.

VmName.description: Unique for one launch: a name is never reused. The Dispatcher's names are `cr-<kind>-<job id>-cf-<8 hex>` (63 characters at most).

SandboxFailureKind.description: `SANDBOX_FAILURE_KINDS` of dispatcher/src/launchers/sandbox-service.ts; a test of the Dispatcher holds the two equal.

InstanceType.description: A Cloudflare Containers instance type the Worker is configured with (`standard-4` today; a larger custom type is configuration only).

Tags.description: Free labels of the VM; the Dispatcher sets `app`, `kind`, `job` and `tenant`. Values are plain text without a colon problem: a filter is `k:v`.

timeoutMs.description: The backstop: the VM is destroyed this long after it was created if nobody deleted it.

CreateVmResponse.description: 201 once the Container runs, the image's boot is done and it accepts `exec`.

ExecRequest.description: A command is an argument vector, never shell text. `sudo` means run as root (the Container's processes run as root anyway; the field is kept for parity with the Vercel port). `label` is a stable name of the step for logs, never the command text.

ExecResponse.description: The command ran to its end (or to `timeoutMs`, then exitCode is 124 and stderr says nothing more). `stdout` and `stderr` are each cut to the last 1048576 bytes (1 MiB).

StartProcessResponse.description: 201: the process runs with its stdin open and outlives the HTTP request (the Durable Object holds it and keeps the Container alive with an alarm).

ProcessState.description: `running: false` carries the exit code (a VM that is stopped under the process: 137). `running: true` after waitMs.

NetworkPolicy.description: `NetworkPolicy` of dispatcher/src/network/rule.ts: everything, nothing, or a list of host names (`*.example.com` is a suffix). The handler of the Container's outbound traffic reads it for every request; private addresses stay refused whatever it says.

ListedVm.description: `ListedVm` of dispatcher/src/launchers/sandbox-service.ts for the reaper. `status` is the Worker's own word (`running`, `pending`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `failed`); the Dispatcher never assumes one it does not know, and reaps `stopped` and `failed` ones with DELETE.

HealthResponse.description: No authentication. `workerFeatures`: the claim features (`KnownClaimFeature` of runner-api.v1.json) the Worker image inside the Container image supports, read from that image at build time like the golden snapshot's manifest; the Dispatcher names an image-gated claim feature only when it is listed here and in its own snapshot. `imageVersion`: the git SHA of the build, logged by the Dispatcher. `instanceTypes`: the types the Worker accepts in CreateVmRequest. `workerImageDigest`: see the description of the document. `sysboxProof`: `proven` or `unproven`.

Paths.description: Not a body: the routes of the API, so that the Worker and the Dispatcher test the same list (`dispatcher/src/launchers/cf-sandbox.test.ts` reads it).
